reviews.reason: Exact source transcription is not established. The scan appears to begin ወእተ, not the candidate’s ውእተ; I also cannot positively verify the candidate’s final ለርእዩ glyph sequence. The printed appearance expression carries both an asterisk and enclosing daggers; fruit is separately dagger-marked. Neither expression is bracketed. The English safely retains appearance and fruit without identifying a species, but that does not resolve the source-glyph discrepancies.
reviews.suggested_text: Then I said, “This is a beautiful tree, beautiful to look at[a]; its leaves are lovely, and its fruit[b] is very pleasing to look at.”
reviews.footnote_changes: a: The printed Ethiopic appearance expression is asterisked and dagger-marked. In p.62 note9 Charles regards the Greek fragrance reading as almost certainly correct; this translation nevertheless follows the printed Ethiopic appearance wording. b: The printed fruit expression is dagger-marked. In p.62 note10 Charles calls it corrupt and proposes flowers, comparing the Greek. This translation retains fruit from the printed main text.

reviews.reason: The English and referent note are safe, but exact source transcription remains unresolved: the opening appears to be ወእተ rather than ውእተ, and I cannot positively match every character of the candidate’s ፩እምነ against the scan. The printed holy-and-honored designation supports retaining both qualities; apparatus note15 records Greek omission of the latter, not deletion from this Ethiopic text. Michael is the accompanying individual and the one over an unnamed plural referent. XXV begins after this unit, so no speech belongs here. No source replacement is supplied without complete glyph verification.
reviews.suggested_text: Then Michael, one of the holy and honored angels, who was with me, answered me—he who was over them.[a]
reviews.footnote_changes: a: Michael is the subject of the accompanying clause and the closing designation. The plural referent of them is not named here. Honored may also be rendered glorious; p.62 note15 records omission of this designation in Greek. His speech begins in chapter25 and is not included here.
